prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you left the game at the start of the fourth quarter to beat traffic. Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the Committee,

I come before you today to address these scurrilous allegations with the full weight of my conscience—and a partial plate of leftover brisket.

Yes. I left in the fourth quarter. I do not deny the *act*. But I categorically reject the *characterization*.

I did not leave to "beat traffic." I left to *honor* traffic—to respect the sacred flow of parking-lot egress that binds us all as a people. To linger would have been selfish. To depart was an act of *civic generosity*.

Let the record reflect: we were down twenty-eight points. The starters had been benched. The mascot had stopped trying. If loving my family enough to get them home before the nachos congealed is un-American, then I ask you—what *is* America?

I have here a signed affidavit from my cousin Gary, who will corroborate that I "watched the rest on my phone in the car," a patriotic compromise embraced by millions of hardworking citizens.

You may subpoena my E-ZPass records. You may cross-examine my tailgate. But you will not, I say *will not*, make me apologize for a well-timed exit.

I yield the remainder of my time, and I ask that the Committee please pass the potato
